Dengue Outbreak Disrupts Oil & Gas Operations in Ecuador

A significant dengue fever outbreak has hit Ecuador’s Oil & Gas Producers industry, with over 200 confirmed cases among workers at extraction and processing sites in the Sucumbíos and Orellana provinces, according to local health authorities. Operations at several facilities, including those managed by AndesPetro and PetroAmazon, have been scaled back since last week as companies struggle to maintain staffing levels.

“It’s the worst health event we have faced in over a decade,” said Juan Carlos Molina, operations manager at AndesPetro, who confirmed that two well pads were temporarily shut down on Monday for deep cleaning and vector control. “We have deployed additional medical teams and are rotating shifts, but the disruption is significant.”

The National Association of Oil & Gas Producers of Ecuador estimates that crude output in the affected areas has dropped by 8% since the outbreak began. “Reduced manpower and quarantine measures are making it difficult to keep production at normal levels,” said association president Lucía Sánchez. “If the outbreak continues, we could see lasting impacts on monthly output targets.”

Union representatives have also raised concerns over worker safety. “We urge all operators to prioritize health protocols and provide protective equipment,” said Ángel Torres, spokesperson for the Oilfield Workers’ Union.

Local authorities have launched mosquito control efforts near camps and processing facilities but warn that high rainfall and remote locations complicate response. “We are coordinating with both public and private operators to contain the outbreak,” said Dr. Elisa Paredes, provincial health director. The situation remains fluid as case numbers continue to climb.
